dedupe_keys.name: openems two stage stochastic and robust ambulance location and routing package austin travis county ems

description: OpenEMS is an open-source pipeline for deciding where ambulances should wait and which calls they should serve, built with Austin-Travis County Emergency Medical Services in Texas. It turns historical calls into a grid of demand, computes travel distances from OpenStreetMap, solves two-stage stochastic and robust linear programs for ambulance stationing and routing, and replays historical calls through a simulation engine that logs each call, arrival on scene and arrival at hospital, with plots and a prototype interface for EMS managers. The provider is Joshua Ong, David Kulpanowski, Yangxinyu Xie, Evdokia Nikolova and Ngoc Mai Tran, who describe it in an arXiv preprint (2022). Coverage is Austin and Travis County, calibrated on the 246,809 calls served in 2019 and 2020 by 37 ambulances; the README explains how to replace the input files with another city's data. The Julia and Python code is on GitHub under the MIT licence, with Jupyter notebooks for each step. Caveats: the last commit was in January 2022, the interface is a prototype, travel times come from road distances, not traffic data, and the preprint reports a change in response time from optimal stationing that should be checked against its full text. Simulation uses: ambulance fleet sizing, station relocation and what-if tests of losing or adding a unit during a surge. Related records: JEMSS (model-jemss) is a Julia EMS simulator, and the NHS ambulance discrete-event model (model-ambulance-des-nhsx) covers a similar problem in England.
